## What landed

**D15 — per-task deadlines (CONFIRMED→repaired).** `hh_w1` set `agent_deadline_ms` 900 000 + `verify_deadline_ms` 600 000 for EVERY cell — reproduced: `crates/hh-runner/src/bin/hh_w1.rs` load_cfg lines (pre-fix anchors ~L147–148). Now `task_toml::load_task_decl` reads `<tasks_dir>/<task>/task.toml` (`[agent].timeout_sec`, `[verifier].timeout_sec`) and `resolve_deadline_ms` applies the pinned Harbor semantics (multiplier 1.0 — the re-proof job config declares no override/max/multiplier; absent → cfg fallback recorded `cfg_default`; the agent deadline bounds `agent.run` only — setup/build are separate ladders in Harbor, matching the drive's undated setup legs). `cell-report.json` records `deadlines.agent/verify.{deadline_ms,deadline_source}` per phase + `verify_attempt`. The ADR-0448 appendix records Harbor's exact source lines.

**D17 — kill the lapsed exec's own tree (CONFIRMED→repaired).** The pre-fix timeout path killed the host `podman exec` client + `terminate_group("agent")` on every phase and returned EMPTY streams — reproduced (Wc7 `query-optimize` H-pub `cell-report.json`: `verifier_unavailable:verifier_timeout`, `verify_attempts: 2`, leaked attempt-1 pytest finishing at ~812 s wrote the collected `reward.txt` = 1 + `ctrf.json` 6/6 under a timed-out verdict). Now `cell::exec_guarded` (shared by `PodmanCell` and `hh_w1`'s `DriveCell`) wraps deadline-bearing execs in `wrap_kill` (`setsid timeout --kill-after`, the admitted AR-22/REQ-XE-119 mechanism), tags each with `-e HH_EXEC_TAG=hh-exec-<n>`, and on lapse: kills the host client, `terminate_exec_tag` (a `/proc/*/environ` fixed-string TERM→KILL walk on `hh-helper`'s `PodmanBackend`), then CONFIRMS death by `exec_tag_alive` before returning — never a cmdline pattern the verifier tree lacks. Streams captured up to the lapse are kept. ST5 collects per-attempt under `collect/attempt-<n>`; top-level `collect/` always names the latest attempt's bytes; `VerifyOutcome.attempt` records the owning attempt. The agent phase re-check: its exec carries the same tag+wrap, so the oracle/agent tree terminates by tag; the ST3 `terminate_group("agent")` sweep stays as REQ-XB-119's recorded second belt (`agent_terminated` fact unchanged). `max_grade_attempts = 2` confirmed against REQ-XB-111 (frozen bound) — unchanged; Harbor at the pin runs the verifier once per trial (job `n_attempts` are whole trials, not same-cell regrades).

**D18 — resource audit.** `docs/build/reports/2026-11-16-fp-cell-resource-audit.json` — HH cells ran `CellSpec::default()` (unbounded, not declared); the fp-wc8 planning bound 6 GiB < `torch-tensor-parallelism`'s declared `memory_mb` 8192. Cells now apply declared `cpus`/`memory_mb` verbatim (Harbor semantics — the declared value IS the container limit): `--cpus 1` + `--memory 2048m|8192m`. Packing re-check recorded: worst 4-cell pack for this member set = 14 336 MiB ≤ 26 624; a set with ≥ 4 heavy declarants re-checks under C × declared-max ≤ memory_gib_available (needs `memory_per_trial_gib ≥ 8` or C ≤ 3).

**D19/A5 — classifier + re-fold.** `reproof::classify_task`: `allowlist_gap{host}` only with a named denied host; H-allow < R/R with `denied_hosts: []` → `DiscordClass::Machinery` qualified `h_allow` → `repair:machinery{h_allow}` (register `machinery{h_allow}`; `fp_prereg::excluded` keeps it non-excluding). `reproof::refold_a5` is the appended re-fold rule; `docs/build/reports/2026-11-16-fp-a5-reclassification.json` re-folds Wc4–Wc8's member verdicts (44 rows, 34 changed — every `{unknown}`/empty-denied gap → `machinery{h_allow}`; Wc4's five named-host gaps stand; Wc5 had no folded verdict; Wc8's early-stop verdicts unchanged).

## Deviations / surfaced items

- Harbor's absent-agent semantics is `None` (unbounded); the drive's cfg fallback applies and records `cfg_default` — the machinery bound is kept, never fabricated as a declaration. A missing `task.toml` FILE is a typed error, not a fallback (a task without its record cannot claim declared deadlines).
- `timeout`'s exit-124 is honored only past the declared deadline — an early 124 stays the phase's own exit code.
- The re-fold is a new dated record (`hh-reclassification/1`); register bytes unchanged (append-only preserved).
